predecessors.name: Kingdom of Lazica
predecessors.text: the north-western strip of Lazica, the Black Sea coast between the Gumista and Bzyb rivers (Cliopatria's Georgia row, 724-777)

successors.name: Kingdom of Abkhazia
successors.text: Abasgia, which Leon II made the core of the Kingdom of Abkhazia ('King of the Abkhazians') when he won his full independence c.

ledger.x: 724: the Abasgian principality stands on the Abkhaz coast at Anacopia, a Byzantine dependency.
724: the north-western coast passes to the Abasgians in the record.

c. 778: Leon II wins full independence from Byzantium and the principality becomes the Kingdom of Abkhazia. 'Towards circa 778, Leon II won his full independence with the help of the Khazars.' The Abasgia infobox gives 'Disestablished: 786' and the Kingdom of Abkhazia page says the state 'was established in the 780s'…

wars.name: Arab expedition of Marwan ibn Muhammad into Abkhazia
wars.outcome: The Arab army 'surged into Abkhazia in 736' but, hit by dysentery and floods and meeting 'a stubborn resistance offered by the archon Leon I and his Iberian and Lazic allies', retreated; no border moved.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary: the Abasgia page names two rivers (Gumista and Bzyb) and one town (Anacopia); the Cliopatria strip is soft throughout.
